ballet.name: Ballet
ballet.where: Italian Renaissance courts in the 1400s and 1500s, shaped in the French court; Louis XIV founded the Académie Royale de Danse in 1661.
ballet.roots: Court dance and spectacle; Pierre Beauchamp set the five positions of the feet; the terms are French.
ballet.people: Marie Taglioni (La Sylphide, 1832, early pointe work), Anna Pavlova, Misty Copeland (first African American female principal dancer at American Ballet Theatre, 2015).
signature: turnout from the hips, long lifted spine, pointed feet.
vertical lines, often high, shown to the front.
ballet.look: Turnout; arms framing the head; the finish of each turn.
ballet.music: A ballet class piano waltz in 3 at 168 beats a minute, counted one count to a bar as ballet classes count a waltz (56 counts a minute).
ballet.caption: Pointe shoes: satin over a hard box, so a dancer can rise onto the tips of the toes.

modern.name: Modern dance
modern.where: United States and Germany, early 1900s, as a break from ballet's rules.
modern.roots: Dancers wanted movement from natural impulses and their own time.
modern.people: Isadora Duncan (bare feet, natural movement), Martha Graham (contraction and release; company founded 1926), Alvin Ailey (Revelations, 1960).
signature: movement led from the torso, bare feet.
low levels and the floor, asymmetry.
may move with, against or without the beat.
weight given to gravity, strong contrasts.
modern.look: The spine curving; weight dropping into the floor; stillness.
modern.music: Sparse piano and low pad, 68 beats a minute.
modern.caption: Bare feet, so the soles can grip, slide and feel the floor.

jazz.name: Jazz dance
jazz.where: United States, 1900s, from African American social dance into theater and film.
jazz.roots: The cakewalk, the Charleston and the Lindy Hop; theatrical jazz from the 1940s.
jazz.people: Jack Cole (theatrical jazz technique), Katherine Dunham, Bob Fosse.
signature: isolations (one body part moves alone), low center.
jazz.look: Isolations; accents that land between beats; a strong finish.
jazz.music: Swung brass-like stabs and walking bass, 120 beats a minute.
jazz.caption: Soft split-sole jazz shoes, made to bend and turn.

tap.name: Tap dance
tap.roots: African American dance (juba, buck dancing) meeting Irish and Scottish step dancing; metal taps from the early 1900s.
tap.people: William Henry Lane, "Master Juba" (1840s), Bill "Bojangles" Robinson, Gregory Hines. National Tap Dance Day is May 25, Robinson's birthday (US Congress, 1989).
signature: shuffles, flaps, heel drops, time steps.
the dancer is a drummer; rhythm and improvisation.
tap.look: Sound over shape; how quiet the top stays; trading phrases.
tap.music: Light swing bass only; the taps are the music, 104 beats a minute.
tap.caption: Metal plates on the toe and heel make every step a sound.

breaking.name: Breaking
breaking.where: The Bronx, New York City, early 1970s, part of hip hop culture.
breaking.roots: At block parties DJ Kool Herc looped the "break" of records; b-boys and b-girls danced to the breaks; battles in a circle (the cypher).
breaking.people: DJ Kool Herc, Rock Steady Crew (1977), and the first Olympic breaking event (Paris 2024).
signature: whole body, hands to the floor.
on the breakbeat; freezes hit the accents.
breaking.look: Going down from standing; the freeze on an accent; style as a signature.
breaking.music: Breakbeat drums with scratch-like sweeps, 110 beats a minute.
breaking.caption: Sneakers on a flattened cardboard square, a slick floor for spins.

irish.name: Irish step dance
irish.where: Ireland; dancing masters taught steps across the country from the 1700s.
irish.roots: Competition (the feis); the Irish Dancing Commission developed competition rules in the early 1930s; Riverdance (Eurovision, Dublin, 1994) took it worldwide.
irish.people: Riverdance's first leads, Jean Butler and Michael Flatley.
signature: upright, arms still at the sides.
light in soft shoes, loud in hard shoes.
irish.look: The still arms; the speed of the feet; crossed feet and turned-out toes.
irish.music: A reel in 4 on a fiddle-like lead, 112 beats a minute.
irish.caption: Soft shoes for light dances and hard shoes, with tips and heels made to strike, for loud ones.

flamenco.name: Flamenco
flamenco.where: Andalusia, southern Spain; on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage since 2010.
flamenco.roots: Grew among Gitano (Roma) communities with many Andalusian influences; three parts: cante (song), toque (guitar), baile (dance).
flamenco.people: Carmen Amaya, Antonio Gades, Sara Baras.
signature: proud upright torso, curving arms (braceo), turning hands (floreo).
compás; soleá and alegrías cycles of 12 counts with accents on 3, 6, 8, 10 and 12.
flamenco.look: How accents fall in the 12; arms against feet; a sharp closing pose.
flamenco.music: Plucked guitar rasgueado with palmas (handclaps), 150 counts a minute.
flamenco.caption: Heeled shoes with rows of small nails in the toe and heel for footwork.

bharatanatyam.name: Bharatanatyam
bharatanatyam.where: Tamil Nadu, South India; reshaped and named in the 1930s.
bharatanatyam.roots: Grew from temple and court dance of hereditary women dancers (sadir), with roots in the Natya Shastra, an ancient treatise on performance; Rukmini Devi Arundale founded Kalakshetra in 1936.
signature: araimandi (half-sitting, knees bent outward), mudras (hand gestures that carry meaning), eyes leading.
adavus (basic step units), striking feet, sculptural poses.
rhythm syllables (tha ka dhi mi) in tala cycles; Adi tala has 8 beats.
crisp pure dance (nritta) and expressive storytelling (abhinaya).
bharatanatyam.look: The triangle of the bent knees; the hands; feet striking with the syllables.
bharatanatyam.music: Barrel-drum-like strokes and small cymbals, Adi tala, 80 beats a minute.
bharatanatyam.caption: Ankle bells (salangai) ring with each strike of the feet.

Body.turnout: Legs rotated out from the hips.
Body.gesture: A movement of a part that does not carry weight.

Action.fall and recovery: Yielding to gravity and regaining balance.
Action.footwork: Patterns and actions made by the feet.

Space.direction and facing: Where movement travels and the body faces.
Space.general space and personal space: The shared area and the space immediately around a dancer.
Space.cypher: The circle of a breaking battle.

Time.syncopation: An accent off the main beat.
Time.unison and canon: Together in time, or the same phrase starting at different times.

Energy.suspended: A sense of hanging before the next movement.

lines.wCritique: Press Note when you see something worth saying. It's stamped to that count.
lines.traceHow: Each ghost is half a count apart. Hands draw solid lines, feet draw dotted ones.
lines.rhythmHow: Tall bars are strong accents. Dots are the sound of the feet.
lines.draftHow: Now tap Insert note under a box, so every claim points to a moment.
lines.i.ballet: Ballet began in Renaissance courts and grew up in France, which is why its words are French.
lines.i.modern: Modern dance broke ballet's rules and let weight, breath and the floor back in.
lines.i.jazz: Jazz dance grew from African American social dance into theater and film.
lines.i.tap: In tap, the dancer is also the drummer. Listen as much as you watch.
lines.i.breaking: Breaking started at Bronx block parties in the 1970s, danced to the breaks of records.
lines.i.irish: Irish step dance keeps the arms still, so all the speed lives in the feet.
lines.i.flamenco: Flamenco joins song, guitar and dance in a cycle of twelve counts.
lines.i.bharatanatyam: Bharatanatyam, from South India, tells stories with the hands and keeps time with the feet.
